minutes.headline: Select Board approved a $3.685M refunding and road bond issue, plus a liquor license change and routine appointments.
minutes.summary: The Select Board, with the acting town manager, heard announcements, then approved a liquor license change for Honey Farms, a charity bike ride and several appointments. The main business was the treasurer's bond sale: refunding of USDA sewer and water bonds and borrowing for road paving. A board member also handed out corrected costs of the teachers' contract.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to authorize refunding bonds and approve the sale of the 2018 municipal purpose loan bonds, with related votes.
The treasurer reported the refunding of USDA sewer and water bonds reduces payments for property owners who pay through betterments.
A premium on the bid for the pavement management bond reduced the amount borrowed, and the premium was applied to the project.
The board approved a liquor license change of beneficial interest and manager for Honey Farms, and a charity bike ride on June 10th.
The board appointed a clock winder and an Agricultural Commission member, and will put an event and entertainment license policy on a future agenda.

why_it_matters: The road bond is repaid over 15 years through the tax rate, so the borrowing affects tax bills for that period, and the refunding lowers payments for some sewer and water betterment payers.
Corrected figures on the cost of the teachers' contract over three years were handed out, which bears on future school budgets and the tax rate.
watch_next: Next meeting is May 1st, with a facilities planning workshop being arranged.
An event and entertainment license policy discussion, including Shady Point's guidelines, is to be placed on a future agenda.
